Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks. We allow 12.0 points a game, and we just won at Michigan in overtime. Full pageant wave."

Tor speaks for Minnesota, cocoa steaming. "Well, we beat Iowa 13-10 on Saturday, and we beat Michigan 20-14 and won at Washington. Maverick Baranowski has 51 tackles. TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks. And our defense doesn't give up much through the air. We're polite, but stubborn."

Why Indiana? Because the Hoosiers have been brutal against teams that can't move the ball. They beat North Texas 52-16, Howard 55-0 and Western Kentucky 38-0 in Bloomington, and won 47-15 at Rutgers. Minnesota's run game has struggled all year, and Indiana's defense allows 12.0 points a game. Purdue beat the Gophers 41-13, and Mississippi State beat them 38-13. My final has Indiana winning by more than three touchdowns.

The risk is the Indiana offense's last two games. Hoover went 20 of 40 in a 19-15 loss to Ohio State, then 8 of 18 for 81 yards at Michigan, where it took overtime to win 13-6. Minnesota's defense is sturdy, and if this turns into a slog, 20.5 is a lot of points to lay.

Floyd's Keepers Head to Bloomington: Minnesota Visits No. 4 Indiana on Halloween

Minnesota (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at No. 4 Indiana (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, Ind., CBS.

Your hosts are Torvald "Tor" Engebretsen, a Minnesota ski-hill Gopher who owns enough coats to lend one out, and Mallory Penhallow, a former Miss Monroe County runner-up who runs a 40-tab efficiency model.

Mallory: Welcome to Bloomington, Tor! Hello, Hoosier Nation!

Tor: Thank you, Mallory. I brought cocoa, and a spare coat in case you get chilly.

Mallory: That's very sweet. I'll wear it over the sash.

Tor: And I should mention we're bringing home a bronze pig. Well, it's already home. We won it Saturday.

Players to watch

Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 116 of 187 for 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. Turbo Richard leads the rushers with 711 yards and six scores, and Charlie Becker leads the receivers with 42 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns. On defense, Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks, and linebacker Isaiah Jones leads the team with 61 tackles.

Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 141 of 222 for 1,472 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. TJ Thomas leads the rushers with 325 yards, and Javon Tracy leads the receivers with 39 catches for 420 yards. Linebacker Maverick Baranowski leads the defense with 51 tackles, and TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks.

Mallory: Nine sacks for Tobi Osunsanmi, Tor. It's the explosives, darling.

Tor: Maverick Baranowski has 51 tackles. In Minnesota, we call that a good catch.

What happened last week

Minnesota beat Iowa 13-10 at home on Oct. 24, on Homecoming, and took back Floyd of Rosedale, the bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. Lindsey threw for 137 yards, and Tracy caught seven balls for 45 yards. The defense did the heavy lifting, holding Iowa to 10 points.

Tor: Floyd is back in Minneapolis. I may have hugged a pig. A bronze one. Respectfully.

Indiana won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan on Oct. 24. Hoover went 8 of 18 for 81 yards, Richard ran 19 times for 68 yards, and the defense held Michigan to six points. It came one week after a 19-15 loss to Ohio State.

Mallory: Grace in defeat one week, grit on the road the next. Full pageant wave.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hoover has thrown the most passes for Indiana in every game, and Lindsey has done the same for Minnesota, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Curt Cignetti was hired at Indiana on Nov. 30, 2023. In 2025, the Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. This year's team allows only 12.0 points a game.

P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017, after coaching Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and coached receivers for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His defense is the strength this year, stingy against the throw and good on third down.

Tor: Coach Fleck rows the boat. We all row together.

Mallory: Coach Cignetti said it best: "It can be done." I have it on a pillow.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Becker and Hoover against a Minnesota defense that allows only 159.7 passing yards a game. On the other side, the Gophers need their big guys up front to open running room against an Indiana defense that allows very little on the ground. Minnesota won the two recent meetings in this series, 38-31 in 2018 and 35-14 in 2021, so the Gophers have some happy memories. Indiana wants to stay near the top of the Big Ten race.

What's happening on campus

A Halloween afternoon in Bloomington means cream and crimson costumes in the stands at Memorial Stadium, and a CBS crowd watching at home. Minnesota fans just finished Homecoming week in Minneapolis, so their voices may still be a little hoarse. Back home, the Gophers play at Huntington Bank Stadium, listed at 50,850 seats.

Tor: I'm dressing as Floyd of Rosedale. Bronze paint and everything.

Mallory: I'm dressing as Miss Congeniality. Wait, that's the sash. I'm giving it to you, Tor, with love.

Anything else fun and true

Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Gophers claim seven national championships. Indiana's 2025 team was the first to win 16 games without a loss since Yale in 1894, and quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman.

Tor: Whatever happens, Mallory, the cocoa's on me afterward. We'll say grace first.

Mallory: Deal, Tor. And keep the coat warm for me.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 34, Minnesota Golden Gophers 11.

Footnotes and Fashion: No. 20 Northwestern Visits Oregon on Halloween

No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) at Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Autzen Stadium, Eugene, Ore., Peacock.

Your hosts are Ezra Lindqvist, a Northwestern data journalist who footnotes his own jokes, and Nix Wyatt-Aldana, a Eugene sneaker-and-uniform designer who reviews jerseys and route trees with equal ferocity.

Nix: Welcome to Autzen, Ezra! Before we begin, I have to review your outfit.

Ezra: I was afraid of that.

Nix: Purple quarter-zip, pumpkin pin for Halloween. Seven out of ten. The pin is carrying you.

Ezra: Footnote: the pin was my mother's idea, and she will be thrilled.

Players to watch

Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 117 of 164 for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and just one interception. Caleb Komolafe leads the rushers with 551 yards and five scores, and Griffin Wilde leads the receivers with 39 catches for 615 yards. Linebacker Braydon Brus leads the defense in both tackles, with 62, and sacks, with four.

For Oregon, Jordon Davison leads the rushers with 422 yards and seven touchdowns, and Dakorien Moore leads the receivers with 34 catches for 417 yards. Dylan Raiola threw the most passes last week, and Lanning has said Brock Thomas and Akili Smith Jr. are in the mix too. On defense, Matayo Uiagalelei has six sacks, and Koi Perich leads the team with 46 tackles.

Ezra: Chiles has one interception in seven games. I checked it three times.

Nix: Uiagalelei rushing the quarterback is pure runway, darling. Ten out of ten.

What happened last week

Northwestern beat Rutgers 42-14 at home on Oct. 24. Chiles threw for 219 yards and three touchdowns, Komolafe ran 13 times for 150 yards and a score, and Wilde caught nine balls for 133 yards and a touchdown.

Ezra: I've already filed my formal correction to everyone who doubted us. It's eleven pages.

Oregon lost 21-10 at Illinois on Oct. 24. Raiola completed 27 of 41 for 246 yards, Davison ran 14 times for 92 yards and the Ducks' touchdown, and Dakorien Moore caught nine balls.

Nix: Honest review? Somebody tripped on the runway. We get back up, we fix the hem.

Injuries and availability

The big news is at quarterback. On Monday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said he doesn't expect Dante Moore back this season. Moore suffered a concussion at USC on Sept. 26 and has missed three games since. Before the injury he was 69 of 99 for 926 yards and nine touchdowns. Raiola and Thomas have started the last three games. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and Chiles has thrown the most passes for Northwestern every week, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Nix: We miss Dante. Get well, kid. You're always on the team.

What the coaches are up to

Lanning also made a change on his staff. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was dismissed Sunday, and assistant coach Jay Johnson will coordinate the offense. Lanning was hired on Dec. 11, 2021, and his 2024 team went 13-1 and 9-0 in the Big Ten, winning the league title in its first season.

David Braun became Northwestern's interim coach in 2023, was named the permanent head coach that November and was the consensus Big Ten Coach of the Year. His team runs the ball and protects it, with only two turnovers lost all season.

Ezra: Two turnovers. Footnote: that's not a typo.

Player storylines

Raiola is the one to watch. He came off the bench against Nebraska, his former team, and threw the winning 4-yard touchdown to tight end Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left. On the other side, Komolafe and Northwestern's big guys up front will test an Oregon defense that allows very little on the ground. These two met last season, and Oregon won 34-14.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Eugene, and Autzen Stadium, opened in 1967 and listed at 54,000 seats, always sounds much bigger than that. Northwestern fans have had a wonderful fall at home. The new Ryan Field opened Oct. 2 against Penn State, exactly 100 years to the day after the original stadium hosted its first game, and the Wildcats have won all four home games.

Nix: I'm dressing as a jersey. A ten-out-of-ten jersey.

Ezra: I'm dressing as a footnote. Very small, very important.

Anything else fun and true

Oregon has played football since 1894, joined the Big Ten in 2024 and went 13-2 last season. Marcus Mariota became Oregon's first Heisman Trophy winner in 2014. Northwestern opened this season with two games at lakefront Martin Stadium, right on Lake Michigan, before moving into the new Ryan Field.

Nix: Whatever happens, Ezra, dinner's on me. We'll say grace first.

Ezra: Deal, Nix. Footnote: I'm holding you to it.

My call: Oregon Ducks 29, Northwestern Wildcats 22.

Trail Shoes and Double Scoops: Colorado State Visits Utah State on Halloween

Colorado State (3-4, 1-2 Pac-12) at Utah State (2-5, 1-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Maverik Stadium, Logan, Utah, USA Net.

Your hosts are Ansel Rimrock, a Colorado State fan who spends his mornings on the foothill trails, and Hyrum Tolleson, a Utah State fan from a Cache Valley dairy who's been up before the sun since he was 8.

Hyrum: Well, hello there, neighbor, and welcome to Logan. Double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream?

Ansel: Hyrum, it's Halloween morning.

Hyrum: Exactly. It's a holiday. Ice cream is the treat, and nobody has to play a trick.

Ansel: Fair enough. Mountain air, thick defense, and one scoop. Just one.

Players to watch

Colorado State quarterback Hauss Hejny threw the most passes in the first two games and again last week. He's 71 of 104 for 952 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. K'saan Farrar threw the most in the four games in between. Mel Brown leads the rushers with 454 yards on just 52 carries, and RJ Vick leads the receivers with 24 catches for 367 yards. Linebacker Oumar Diomande leads the defense with 67 tackles.

Utah State quarterback Grady Brosterhous has thrown the most passes in six straight games. He's 99 of 178 for 1,120 yards, seven touchdowns and six interceptions. Javen Jacobs leads the rushers with 435 yards, and Eli Wood leads the receivers with 37 catches for 479 yards and five touchdowns. Safety Brevin Hamblin leads the defense with 58 tackles, and Jordan Pendleton has 2.5 sacks.

Ansel: Mel Brown runs like he's coming downhill on a switchback. Every carry.

Hyrum: Eli Wood is a fine young man. Catches everything, says thank you after.

What happened last week

Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49 at home on Oct. 24. Hejny threw for 333 yards and three touchdowns, Durell Robinson ran for two scores, and Tommy Maher caught six balls for 108 yards and two touchdowns.

Ansel: A long climb with a big view at the top. I'll take it.

Utah State lost 20-17 at Texas State on Oct. 24, on Homecoming night in San Marcos. Brosterhous threw for 206 yards, and Anthony Garcia caught eight balls for 87 yards.

Hyrum: Three points. That one stung like a cold barn in January. We milk the cows and go again.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hejny threw the most passes for Colorado State last week, and Brosterhous has done it for Utah State in six straight games, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jim Mora was hired at Colorado State on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season. His offense can move the ball and takes care of it, with only four turnovers all season. The defense is the work in progress, and Mora has kept his team swinging, as last week's shootout showed.

Bronco Mendenhall leads Utah State, with a hire date of Dec. 6, 2024. His Aggie defense has kept games close, including a 16-14 loss at Washington and a 17-16 win over Washington State. The offense is the piece he's still building.

Ansel: Coach Mora has been around. Calm on the switchbacks.

Hyrum: Coach Mendenhall works like a dairy farmer. Early mornings, no complaints.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Colorado State's run game against a Utah State defense that has been steady all season. Brown has been breaking long runs, and the Aggies' big guys up front need to keep him in front of them. On the other side, Brosterhous and Wood need to find the end zone against a Rams defense that has had a hard time. Utah State won five of the eight meetings from 2016 through 2025, but Colorado State won the last one, 42-37 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Cache Valley, and Maverik Stadium, home since 1968, is listed at 25,513 seats. The field is named for Merlin Olsen, the Pro Football Hall of Famer who played at Utah State. This is Colorado State's first season in the Pac-12, and the Rams play their home games at Canvas Stadium, opened in 2017 and listed at 36,500.

Hyrum: I'm dressing as a dairy cow. Very traditional.

Ansel: I'm dressing as a trail marker. Follow me, folks.

Anything else fun and true

Utah State football started in 1892, one of the oldest programs in the western United States, and the Aggies have won 13 conference championships across four leagues, most recently in 2021, when they went 11-3. Colorado State spent 49 seasons, from 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium before moving to Canvas.

Hyrum: Whatever happens, Ansel, the ice cream's on me. We'll say grace first.

Ansel: Deal, Hyrum. Make it a double after all.

My call: Utah State Aggies 34, Colorado State Rams 27.

UTEP (1-6, 0-3 Mountain West) at North Dakota State (6-2, 3-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Fargodome, Fargo, N.D., MW+.

Your hosts are Neto Galindo, a UTEP fan and Sun Bowl ironworker's kid who grades effort by chile heat, and Inga Halvorsen, a North Dakota State fan and agricultural economist who has tracked every Bison title since she was a girl.

Inga: Oh, for cute, you made it to Fargo! Welcome, Neto.

Neto: Thanks, Inga. I brought green chile from El Paso. It's Halloween, so I figured I'd bring the scariest thing I own.

Inga: And I brought tater tot hotdish. I bring hotdish either way, hon.

Neto: Then let's make it Hatch-hot hotdish. Neighbors share.

Players to watch

North Dakota State quarterback Nathan Hayes has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 123 of 196 for 1,470 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Myles Mitchell leads the rushers with 393 yards, and Jackson Williams leads the receivers with 32 catches for 503 yards. Linebacker Donovan Woolen leads the defense with 55 tackles, and Kelton McCaslin has four sacks.

For UTEP, Raymond Moore III has thrown the most passes the last two games and leads the team in rushing with 414 yards. EJ Colson Jr. threw the most in the first five games and leads in passing with 628 yards and seven touchdowns. Kam Thomas leads the receivers with 270 yards, linebacker Isaiah Bogerty leads the defense with 42 tackles, and Sterling Miles has 3.5 sacks.

Inga: Against Nevada, Jackson Williams caught a missed field goal in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards. That young man deserves extra hotdish.

Neto: Raymond Moore III runs like a five-alarm chile. Effort grade: Hatch-hot.

What happened last week

North Dakota State lost 21-16 at New Mexico on Oct. 24, on Homecoming weekend in Albuquerque. Hayes threw for 198 yards and two touchdowns, and Williams caught four balls for 71 yards. It was the first meeting on record between the schools.

Inga: Oh, yah, that's a tough one. I made a second hotdish on the bus.

UTEP had an open week. The Miners last played on Oct. 17, losing 24-11 to San José State at the Sun Bowl. Moore threw for 195 yards, and Thomas caught four balls for 96 yards.

Neto: A week off to rest the legs and sharpen the effort. We'll be fresh.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hayes has thrown the most passes for North Dakota State every week, and Moore has done it for UTEP the last two games, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Tim Polasek leads North Dakota State, with a hire date of Dec. 17, 2023. His team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away. The Bison allow 12.5 points a game, they've taken the ball away 14 times, and they shut out Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0.

Scotty Walden leads UTEP, with a hire date of Dec. 4, 2023. His offense runs the ball on most plays, and his team's best day came Sept. 12, a 51-10 win over Texas Southern. The open week gave his staff extra time to prepare.

Inga: Coach Polasek is Fargo through and through. Practical, like a good snow shovel.

Neto: Coach Walden is building it brick by brick, like my dad on a Sun Bowl job site.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is North Dakota State's defense against Moore, who can hurt you with his legs. The Bison's big guys up front have been tough to run on all season. On the other side, Hayes wants a clean day after five interceptions in the two losses, and UTEP's defense will try to force him into more mistakes. This is the first meeting between these schools in our records from 2016 through 2025.

What's happening on campus

Halloween in Fargo means bundling up, and the Fargodome, opened in 1992 and listed at 18,700 seats, keeps everybody warm and loud inside. UTEP fans call the Sun Bowl home, built in 1963 and listed at 51,500, with the Sound of the Southwest band and mascot Paydirt Pete.

Neto: I'm dressing as Paydirt Pete. Pickaxe and all.

Inga: I'm dressing as a casserole dish. Very warm, very Fargo.

Anything else fun and true

North Dakota State has won 18 national championships, including 10 FCS titles between 2011 and 2024, and 39 conference championships. The Bison went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1 in their last five Missouri Valley seasons. UTEP's fight song is "El Paso Fight."

Inga: Whatever happens, Neto, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Neto: Deal, Inga. Share the chile, and the hotdish.

Cafecito in Lynchburg: FIU Visits Liberty on Halloween

FIU (3-4, 1-2 Conference USA) at Liberty (6-1, 3-0 Conference USA). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Williams Stadium, Lynchburg, Va., CBSSN.

Your hosts are Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, an FIU fan from Sweetwater who learned football from her abuela with cafecito and dominoes, and Gideon Fairweather, a Lynchburg youth pastor who coaches middle-school football on the side.

Gideon: Welcome to Lynchburg, Lourdes! Game day here feels like a family reunion with a marching band.

Lourdes: Gracias, Gideon. I brought cafecito and my abuela's dominoes.

Gideon: Dominoes? On Halloween?

Lourdes: The dominoes are the players, the sugar packets are the defense. It's the scariest playbook in Miami.

Players to watch

Liberty quarterback Deshawn Purdie has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 80 of 133 for 1,226 yards and nine touchdowns, and he hasn't thrown an interception all season. Kam Davis leads the rushers with 583 yards and five scores, and Makai Jackson leads the receivers with 23 catches for 540 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Derrell Farrar leads the defense with 39 tackles, and Brenton Williams has three sacks.

FIU quarterback JJ Kohl has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 131 of 227 for 1,637 yards, 10 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Devonte Lyons leads the rushers with 383 yards, and Maguire Anderson leads the receivers with 36 catches for 568 yards. DeeJay Holmes Jr. has five sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads the team with 37 tackles.

Gideon: Zero interceptions for Purdie. I preach a whole sermon on patience, and that young man is living it.

Lourdes: DeeJay Holmes Jr. gets to the quarterback like my abuela gets to the last pastelito. Fast.

What happened last week

Liberty won 34-6 at Kennesaw State on Thursday, Oct. 22. Purdie threw for 176 yards and a touchdown, and Davis ran for a score. Kennesaw State had won the last three meetings, so this one meant plenty.

Gideon: Grace and grit, Lourdes. Grace and grit.

FIU lost 26-23 to Middle Tennessee at home on Tuesday, Oct. 20, a "Paws at the Pit" night. Kohl threw three touchdowns, Lyons ran 19 times for 115 yards, and Kyle McNeal caught a scoring ball. The week before, the Panthers lost 27-24 at Jacksonville State.

Lourdes: Two three-point losses in a row. My abuela needed two coladas. Then she said, "Mija, next week."

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Purdie has thrown the most passes for Liberty every week, and Kohl has done the same for FIU, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jamey Chadwell has led Liberty since the 2023 season, after head coaching stops at North Greenville, Delta State, Charleston Southern and Coastal Carolina. His first Liberty team went 13-1. This year's Flames run the ball and play defense, allowing 14.0 points a game.

Willie Simmons is in his second year at FIU. In his first season, the Panthers went 7-6 and made their first bowl trip since 2019. Before that, he won a black college national championship and a SWAC title at Florida A&M in 2023. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel.

Gideon: Coach Chadwell builds a team the way I build a youth group. Steady, with a lot of snacks.

Lourdes: Coach Simmons wins everywhere he goes. ¡Vamos!

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Davis and Liberty's big guys up front against an FIU defense that allows only 16.3 points a game. On the other side, Kohl needs to find Anderson against a Liberty defense that has been stingy all season. These teams have met four times since 2020. Liberty won three, but FIU won the most recent one, 34-27 last season.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween afternoon in Lynchburg, and Williams Stadium, built in 1989 and listed at 25,000, should be full of Flames fans, plus a costume or two. FIU's Pitbull Stadium, opened in 1995, is listed at 20,000, and its Homecoming is still to come later this fall.

Lourdes: I'm dressing as a domino. Double six. The best one.

Gideon: I'm dressing as a middle-school water bottle. That's what those kids care about most.

Anything else fun and true

Liberty moved from FCS to FBS and became a full member in 2019. In 2020 the Flames entered the AP poll for the first time, at No. 25, and they joined Conference USA in 2023. FIU shared the 2010 Sun Belt championship and plays Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl.

Gideon: Whatever happens, Lourdes, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Lourdes: Deal, Gideon. I'll bring the cafecito.

My call: Liberty Flames 27, Florida International Panthers 12.

Pearls and an Optimism Counter: Southern Miss Visits UL Monroe on Halloween

Southern Miss (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at UL Monroe (1-6, 1-2 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe, La., ESPN+.

Your hosts are Dee Broussard, a Southern Miss fan and former sorority president who calls everybody "sugar" and means it, and Darnell Vidrine, a UL Monroe fan and overnight Delta radio host who keeps an optimism counter running all season.

Darnell: Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is! Welcome to Monroe, Dee.

Dee: Thank you, sugar. Is that the famous optimism counter?

Darnell: Set to 100, like every week. But this week, Dee, I didn't have to reset it. We WON.

Dee: Well, bless it. Congratulations, Darnell. Truly.

Players to watch

Southern Miss quarterback Landry Lyddy has thrown the most passes in the last five games. He's 101 of 170 for 1,196 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Steven Robinson leads the rushers with 577 yards and eight scores, and Mario Sanders leads the receivers with 40 catches for 569 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Mathis Haygood leads the defense with 63 tackles, and Jameer Lewis has four sacks.

UL Monroe quarterback Aidan Armenta has thrown the most passes in the last four games. He's 96 of 153 for 1,121 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Austin Carlisle, who threw the most passes in the second and third games, leads the team in rushing with 237 yards, and Marcellus Jackson leads the receivers with 32 catches. Linebacker Noah Flemmings leads the defense with 65 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has three sacks.

Dee: Steven Robinson runs like he's late for a formal. Eight touchdowns, sugar.

Darnell: Noah Flemmings has 65 tackles. I can FEEL it every time he hits somebody.

What happened last week

UL Monroe won its first game of the season, 21-14 at Troy on Oct. 24, on Troy's Military Appreciation day. Armenta went 13 of 22 for 147 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions.

Darnell: I KNEW IT! I may have sniffled on the air. Okay, I definitely sniffled.

Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31 on Homecoming at "The Rock" on Oct. 24. Jamarice Wilder ran 13 times for 154 yards and a touchdown, and Sanders caught six balls for 77 yards.

Dee: Homecoming win at home. To the top, y'all! I pointed skyward so hard I lost an earring.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Lyddy has thrown the most passes for Southern Miss in five straight games, and Armenta has done it for UL Monroe in four straight, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Blake Anderson is in his first season at Southern Miss, with a hire date of Dec. 11, 2025. His team throws it well and just got a big day from the run game, too. The defense is the work in progress, but the Golden Eagles found a way against Louisiana.

Bryant Vincent leads UL Monroe, with a hire date of Dec. 5, 2023. Two of his team's early losses were one-score games, 26-20 at UAB and 38-35 to SE Louisiana, and last week his defense held Troy to 14 points.

Dee: Coach Anderson walked in and got to work. I respect a man with a plan.

Darnell: Coach Vincent keeps the faith. He's a counter-reset kind of coach.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is the Southern Miss run game against a UL Monroe defense that has had a hard time stopping the run. Robinson and Wilder will test the Warhawks' big guys up front. On the other side, Armenta wants another clean day after throwing for 362 yards at South Alabama earlier this season. Southern Miss won four of the six meetings since 2017, including 49-21 last season, but UL Monroe won 38-21 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Monroe, and Malone Stadium, opened in 1978 and listed at 27,617 seats, gets the home crowd back after last week's trip to Troy. Southern Miss fans just celebrated Homecoming at The Rock, which wears a new name this fall, Renasant Stadium. The nickname isn't going anywhere.

Dee: I'm dressing as a string of pearls. Elegant, timeless, a little bit sparkly.

Darnell: I'm dressing as a 2 a.m. radio show. Everybody's welcome to call in.

Anything else fun and true

UL Monroe football dates to 1931. The school's teams were the Northeast Louisiana Indians for a long stretch and became the Warhawks in 2006, and the program moved up to what is now FBS in 1994. Southern Miss went 7-6 last season, a lovely bounce back after a 1-11 year in 2024.

Darnell: Whatever happens, Dee, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Dee: Deal, sugar. I'll bring the sweet tea.

My call: Southern Miss Golden Eagles 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 26.

Skyline Abernathy is spooning chili onto a plate of spaghetti outside Nippert Stadium when Aspen Mortensen walks up in a ski jacket. "Five-way?" he asks. "Onions and beans. Reserved for greatness." Aspen eyes the plate. "Send it, no fear," she says, grabbing a fork. "But I'm warning you, Skyline. There will be avalanche puns."

No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) visits Cincinnati (5-2, 2-2 Big 12) Saturday at 3:45 p.m. ET on ESPN at Nippert Stadium. DraftKings has Utah Utes −6.5 with a total of 56.5. On Monday, DraftKings had Utah −6.5 and 55.5. My card: Utah Utes −6.5, Over 56.5, and a final of Utah Utes 33, Cincinnati Bearcats 25.

Aspen speaks for Utah. "We beat Houston 21-13 last week for our first win ever over the Cougars. Devon Dampier ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns. He has 15 touchdown throws, Wayshawn Parker has eight rushing touchdowns, and Braden Pegan has six receiving touchdowns. We allow 14.6 points a game. That's a black-diamond defense."

Skyline speaks for Cincinnati. "We beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24 last week, only the third top-10 win in Nippert Stadium history. JC French threw four touchdowns, and Cole Tabb ran for 173 yards. French has only two interceptions all season. Tabb has nine rushing touchdowns. Five-way, no hesitation."

Why Utah? Because the Utes do everything well. They've beaten Arkansas 43-10, Utah State 33-0 and Kansas 41-24, and they allowed 13 points to Houston. Utah allows 14.6 points a game while scoring 37.4, and Dampier has thrown and run for big plays all season. My final has the Utes winning by eight.

The risk is that Cincinnati is rolling at home. The Bearcats score 35.4 points a game, and Tabb has 621 rushing yards on just 65 carries. Utah won its last two games 27-24 at Colorado and 21-13 against Houston, and Dampier threw two interceptions in each. Utah starting offensive lineman Kelvin Obot was hurt at Colorado and missed Houston, and coach Morgan Scalley says there's no timetable.

Why the Over? Cincinnati doesn't play many quiet games. The Bearcats lost 45-42 at West Virginia, beat Miami (OH) 35-31 and scored 37 against Texas Tech. Utah scored 66 against Idaho, 43 against Arkansas and 41 against Kansas. Cincinnati allows 26.4 points a game, and Utah should get its share. My 33-25 adds up to 58, over 56.5.

Now the room. The Formula has Utah 32-25 and sides with Utah and the Over. Next Man Up has Utah 34-25 and lands on Utah and the Over. Follow The Money likes Cincinnati after the spread came down from where it opened, and sits out the total since it hasn't budged. In The Trenches sits out: the Utah run game and the Cincinnati run game each have a matchup they like, so they cancel out.

Follow The Money said it plainly: "The market moved toward Cincinnati. I go with the market."

Next Man Up shook his head: "Utah is unbeaten for a reason."

The Formula shrugged: "Utah by a touchdown and change."

Bottom of the card: an unbeaten Utah team with a top defense, a Cincinnati offense that scores in bunches and a Nippert crowd still buzzing from last week. Give me the Utes and the Over.

Utah Utes 33, Cincinnati Bearcats 25. Utah Utes cover the 6.5. Over 56.5.

Chili and Slalom Gates: No. 6 Utah Visits Cincinnati on Halloween

No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) at Cincinnati (5-2, 2-2 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati, ESPN.

Your hosts are Aspen Mortensen, a Utah fan and former ski racer who reads defenses like slalom gates, and Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy, a Cincinnati engineering co-op kid who ranks everything in chili ways.

Skyline: Welcome to Nippert, Aspen! Two Saturdays, two top-10 visitors. That's a five-way schedule.

Aspen: Thanks, Skyline. I'll warn you now, there will be avalanche puns.

Skyline: I can handle puns. Can your defense handle Cole Tabb?

Aspen: Our defense eats gates for breakfast. Send it, no fear.

Players to watch

Utah quarterback Devon Dampier has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 136 of 198 for 1,616 yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he ran for 150 yards and two scores last week. Wayshawn Parker leads the rushers with 644 yards and eight touchdowns, and Braden Pegan leads the receivers with 34 catches for 459 yards and six scores. Linebacker Trey Reynolds leads the defense with 44 tackles, and Karson Kaufusi has two sacks.

Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 127 of 183 for 1,510 yards, 13 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Cole Tabb leads the rushers with 621 yards and nine scores on just 65 carries, and JV Gibson leads the receivers with 29 catches for 385 yards. Linebacker Jonathan Thompson leads the defense with 60 tackles, and Patrick Bauer has three and a half sacks.

Aspen: Dampier runs like he's on a fresh powder day. Nobody catches him.

Skyline: Nine touchdowns for Tabb on 65 carries. That's onions AND beans.

What happened last week

Utah beat Houston 21-13 at home on Oct. 24, the Utes' first win ever over the Cougars. Dampier threw for 204 yards and ran for 150 more with two touchdowns.

Aspen: Five losses to Houston, then finally a win. Every ski run has a bottom, and we made it to the lodge.

Cincinnati beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24 on Homecoming in front of a sold-out Nippert crowd. French threw four touchdowns, and Tabb ran 16 times for 173 yards and a score. It was only the third top-10 win in Nippert Stadium history.

Skyline: Five-way. Extra onions. I'm still smiling.

Injuries and availability

The official Big 12 availability report hasn't been posted yet. Utah coach Morgan Scalley said starting offensive lineman Kelvin Obot, who was hurt at Colorado and missed the Houston game, has no timetable and is getting a second opinion. Cincinnati coach Scott Satterfield said the team is close to getting starting nose tackle Josh Hough back after he missed last week, and starting center Taran Tyo, who left last week's game, likely won't have an answer until late in the week. Check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Morgan Scalley is in his first season as Utah's head coach after taking over in December 2025. He played defensive back for the Utes from 2001 to 2004, joined the staff in 2007 and spent 10 seasons as defensive coordinator. After the Colorado win he said, "It's not always pretty, but we did enough."

Scott Satterfield became Cincinnati's 43rd head coach on Dec. 5, 2022. His offense runs the ball well and almost never gives it away.

Aspen: Coach Scalley has been a Ute for a long time. He knows every gate on this course.

Skyline: Coach Satterfield has us at a five-way. I'm not downgrading anything this week.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Tabb and the Cincinnati big guys up front against a Utah defense that allows only 14.6 points a game. On the other side, Dampier and Parker face a Bearcats defense that just slowed down Texas Tech. These teams met for the first time last season, on Nov. 1 in Salt Lake City, where College GameDay was in town, and Utah won 45-14.

What's happening on campus

For the first time in program history, Cincinnati is hosting ranked opponents in back-to-back weeks, and it all happens on Halloween. Football has been played on the Nippert site since 1901, which Cincinnati calls the second-oldest playing site in college football.

Aspen: I'm dressing as an avalanche. Big, fast and loud.

Skyline: I'm dressing as a five-way. Onions and beans included.

Anything else fun and true

Utah football began in 1892 and has played on the current site of Rice-Eccles Stadium since 1927. The Utes have won two BCS bowls, the 2005 Fiesta Bowl and the 2009 Sugar Bowl. Cincinnati became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff in the 2021 season, when the Bearcats played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl.

Skyline: Whatever happens, Aspen, chili's on me. We'll say grace first.

Aspen: Deal, Skyline. I'll bring the fry sauce.

My call: Utah Utes 33, Cincinnati Bearcats 25.

Bow Ties and Rolled Trees: Virginia Visits No. 14 Wake Forest on Halloween

Virginia (4-4, 2-3 ACC) at No. 14 Wake Forest (6-1, 4-1 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem, N.C., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Prescott Ashby-Lowell, a fourth-generation Wahoo in a game-day bow tie who refuses to say "campus," and Eloise Brightman-Rowe, a Wake Forest grad and debate-team darling who rolls the Quad and politely roasts bad tackling.

Eloise: Welcome to Winston-Salem, Prescott! Resolved: Wake Forest is the best place to spend Halloween.

Prescott: I'll accept the premise, Eloise, with one amendment. The Grounds are a close second.

Eloise: Two minutes for rebuttal.

Prescott: I only need one. Go 'Hoos.

Players to watch

Wake Forest quarterback Gio Lopez has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 140 of 207 for 1,947 yards, 17 touchdowns and just one interception. Carlos Hernandez leads the receivers with 49 catches for 720 yards and four scores, and Ty Clark III leads the rushers with 328 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker Vincent Firenze leads the defense with 49 tackles, and Langston Hardy has five and a half sacks.

Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 119 of 183 for 1,369 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. Jekail Middlebrook leads the rushers with 513 yards and four scores, and Da'Shawn Martin has five touchdown catches. Matthew Fobbs-White has four sacks, and cornerback Jacobie Henderson leads the team with 40 tackles.

Eloise: One interception all season. Gio Lopez would win any debate about ball security.

Prescott: Mr. Fobbs-White has four sacks. Mr. Jefferson would've charted every one.

What happened last week

Wake Forest had an open date. The Demon Deacons' last game was a 41-7 win at Cal on Oct. 17, when Lopez threw four touchdowns and Dominick Barry caught four balls for 102 yards and three scores. Their only loss this season came against Miami, 33-20.

Eloise: The open week was for rest, film and a little extra Quad rolling.

Virginia lost 19-16 to Duke at Scott Stadium on Friday, Oct. 23. Middlebrook ran 24 times for 117 yards and a touchdown, and John Rogers caught five balls for 65 yards.

Prescott: A close one. I straightened my bow tie and went home to think.

Injuries and availability

The official ACC availability report hasn't been posted yet. Virginia coach Tony Elliott said starting safety Brandyn Hillman and safety Ethan Minter are day-to-day, and he confirmed that Pribula remains the starting quarterback. Hernandez was banged up in the Cal game, and Wake Forest used the open week to heal, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jake Dickert leads Wake Forest, with a hire date of Dec. 18, 2024. His team scores 37.4 points a game, and the defense has 18 sacks. The Demon Deacons beat Louisville on the road and have won their last three ACC games by at least 24 points.

Tony Elliott has led Virginia since being hired Dec. 10, 2021. Before that he coached at Clemson from 2011 to 2021, finishing as associate head coach and offensive coordinator, and he won the 2017 Broyles Award as the top assistant in college football. He also played wide receiver at Clemson. Last season his Cavaliers went 11-3.

Eloise: Coach Dickert's team has won four straight since the Miami game. That's a winning argument.

Prescott: Coach Elliott built an 11-win season. I had it framed.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Lopez and Hernandez against a Virginia defense that allows 19.6 points a game. On the other side, Middlebrook and Virginia's big guys up front need to keep Hardy away from Pribula. Wake Forest won four of the five meetings since 2016, including 16-9 last season, but Virginia won a 31-30 thriller in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Winston-Salem, and Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, built in 1968 and listed at 31,500 seats, gets the Demon Deacons back after the open week. The Spirit of the Old Gold & Black will play "O' Here's to Wake Forest," and rolling the Quad is the tradition every Deacon fan shows visitors first.

Prescott: I'm dressing as Mr. Jefferson. Bow tie, of course.

Eloise: I'm dressing as a rolled tree. Very festive, very white.

Anything else fun and true

Virginia football started in 1887, and Scott Stadium sits next to the university's Academical Village, part of a World Heritage Site. In 1915 Virginia became the first Southern program to beat Yale, winning 10-0 at the Yale Bowl. Before Duke, all three of Virginia's losses came away from Scott Stadium.

Eloise: Whatever happens, Prescott, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Prescott: Splendid, Eloise. I'll bring the bagels.

My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 30, Virginia Cavaliers 19.

display.story_text:
Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz is sketching a game-week roadmap on a whiteboard outside CEFCU Stadium when Paloma Begaye-Ortiz walks up holding two foil-wrapped burritos. "Red or green?" Paloma asks. Tessa studies them like a product spec. "Can I A/B test both?" Paloma laughs. "Both, Tessa. Always both."

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) visits San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West) Saturday at 4 p.m. ET on MW+ at CEFCU Stadium in San Jose. DraftKings has New Mexico Lobos −14.5 with a total of 42.5. My card: New Mexico Lobos −14.5, Over 42.5, and a final of New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

Paloma speaks for New Mexico. "We beat North Dakota State 21-16 last week, and Kiefer Sibley ran for 91 yards and a touchdown. Scottre Humphrey has nine rushing touchdowns, Brett Karhu has five sacks, and Mercury Swaim has 43 tackles. Our defense allows 11.3 points a game. Red or green? BOTH!"

Tessa speaks for San José State. "Rollback. We lost 28-13 at Nevada, and our quarterback spot is a work in progress. Daniel Rolovich got hurt early, and Luke Weaver came back late. Weaver has 11 touchdown throws. Carson Clark has 47 catches, Jayland McGlothen has six sacks and Dylan Lee has 71 tackles. And we've won the last four meetings."

Why New Mexico? Because the Lobos defend and run the ball. New Mexico allows 11.3 points a game, and its only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma. San José State scored 13 points at Nevada and 13 against Wyoming, and it's sorting out its quarterbacks. My final has the Lobos winning by 16.

The risk is the New Mexico passing game. Toa Fa'avae threw for 92 yards last week and 59 at Hawai'i, with interceptions in both, and the Lobos won those games 21-10 and 21-16. McGlothen can get after the quarterback, and the Spartans have won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season. If New Mexico can't throw, this stays close.

Why the Over? New Mexico can score in a hurry: 38 against Central Michigan, 70 against Mercyhurst, 42 at New Mexico State and 61 against UTEP. The last five meetings between these teams finished 48-41, 32-21, 38-21, 52-24 and 35-28. My 31-15 adds up to 46, over 42.5.

Now the room. The Formula has New Mexico 31-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Next Man Up has New Mexico 30-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Follow The Money sits out both, since the spread and the total haven't budged. In The Trenches sits out: the New Mexico run game and the San José State run game each have a matchup they like, so they cancel out.

The Formula opened: "New Mexico's defense wins this by more than two scores."

Next Man Up agreed: "And the Lobos score enough for the Over."

Follow The Money shrugged: "Nothing moved. I'm watching."

Bottom of the card: a New Mexico defense that takes the ball away, a San José State team sorting out its quarterbacks and a Halloween crowd in San Jose. Give me the Lobos and the Over.

Balloons and Product Launches: New Mexico Visits San José State on Halloween

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) at San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4 p.m. ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose, Calif., MW+.

Your hosts are Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, a New Mexico fan who flies a hot-air balloon in the Balloon Fiesta every October, and Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, a San José State fan and tech product lead who treats game week like a launch.

Tessa: Welcome to San Jose, Paloma! I've got the roadmap, the standup and the retro all scheduled.

Paloma: Thanks, Tessa. I brought green chile. Red, too. Both!

Tessa: Can I A/B test them?

Paloma: You can, but the answer is always both.

Players to watch

New Mexico quarterback Toa Fa'avae has thrown the most passes in the last six games. He's 49 of 87 for 790 yards, five touchdowns and four interceptions. Scottre Humphrey leads the rushers with 453 yards and nine scores, and tight end Cade Keith leads the receivers with 20 catches for 265 yards. Brett Karhu has five sacks, and linebacker Mercury Swaim leads the defense with 43 tackles.

San José State's Luke Weaver threw the most passes in each of the first six games and leads the team with 1,620 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jabari Bates leads the rushers with 586 yards, and freshman Carson Clark leads the receivers with 47 catches for 551 yards and five scores. Jayland McGlothen has six sacks, and linebacker Dylan Lee leads the team with 71 tackles.

Paloma: Humphrey runs like a balloon catching a thermal. Up and up.

Tessa: Carson Clark has 47 catches as a freshman. That's a feature I'd demo to anybody.

What happened last week

New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16 on Homecoming in Albuquerque on Oct. 24, during a Pack Week that honored the Route 66 centennial. Kiefer Sibley ran 13 times for 91 yards and a touchdown, and Keith caught five balls.

Paloma: Too much heat for a while, then we soared. Red or green? BOTH!

San José State lost 28-13 at Nevada on Oct. 24. Viliami Teu ran for a touchdown, and Dominique McKenzie caught two balls for 60 yards.

Tessa: Rollback. I opened a bug ticket on the bus ride home.

Injuries and availability

No official Mountain West availability report has been posted for this game yet. San José State's quarterback spot is the big question. Freshman Daniel Rolovich started the last two games, but he was hurt in the first quarter at Nevada, and Weaver came back in the fourth quarter to lead a late scoring drive. Who starts Saturday hasn't been announced, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jason Eck leads New Mexico, with a hire date of Dec. 16, 2024. His defense allows 11.3 points a game and had taken the ball away 21 times through six games. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma.

Ken Niumatalolo was hired at San José State on Jan. 21, 2024. Before the UTEP game he went with Rolovich because, as he put it, the staff "just felt like we needed a spark." He also said of the freshman, "He's got a big arm. He's big and strong and can run. He's not afraid."

Paloma: Coach Eck builds a defense the way I pack a balloon basket. Nothing loose.

Tessa: Coach Niumatalolo ships fixes fast. I respect that.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Humphrey and the New Mexico big guys up front against a Spartans defense that allows 22.5 points a game. On the other side, whoever plays quarterback for San José State has to find Clark against a Lobos defense that loves taking the ball away. San José State has won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season, and the Spartans are looking for an eighth straight home win over the Lobos.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in San Jose, and San José State is hosting Trick or Treat with the Spartans and Youth Spirit Day. Families can trick-or-treat before kickoff, and local youth dance and cheer groups will perform on the field at halftime. CEFCU Stadium opened in 1933 as Spartan Stadium and is listed at 30,456 seats.

Paloma: I'm dressing as a hot-air balloon. Cherry and silver, of course.

Tessa: I'm dressing as a software update. Nobody knows when I'll arrive.

Anything else fun and true

San José State first played a regular season in 1898, and the Spartans count Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil among their alumni. New Mexico's University Stadium opened in 1960, and last season the Lobos went 9-4.

Tessa: Whatever happens, Paloma, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Paloma: Deal, Tessa. I'll bring the green chile.

My call: New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

display.fanatic_story:
Halloween in Norman: South Carolina Visits Oklahoma

South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at Oklahoma (4-3, 2-2 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4:15 p.m. ET (3:15 p.m. CT), Memorial Stadium, Norman, Oklahoma, SEC Network.

Your hosts are Beaumont "Beau" Cheraw, a Gamecock superfan who times everything to dramatic music, including breakfast, and Savannah Redbird-Lowe, a former Oklahoma rodeo princess who reads defenses like barrel patterns.

Beau: (Lights down. Spotlight. Smoke machine, family-sized.) Savannah, I've driven all the way to Norman. I brought the entrance music.

Savannah: Boomer! (You say Sooner.) Welcome back, Beau, sugar. Last time y'all were here, you left with a smile.

Players to watch

South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers has completed 133 of 219 throws for 1,548 yards, with 13 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he runs it too. Running back Matt Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns on 90 carries. Wide receiver Mazeo Bennett Jr. leads the team with 31 catches for 324 yards. Linebacker Justin Okoronkwo leads the defense with 53 tackles.

Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer has completed 136 of 204 throws for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns. Wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III has 41 catches for 578 yards. Linebacker Owen Heinecke has 53 tackles, and defensive lineman Adepoju Adebawore has four sacks.

Savannah: Sategna is my barrel racer. Clean turns, top speed.

What happened last week

South Carolina beat No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 at Williams-Brice Stadium, and it was a thriller. Trailing 24-17 late, the defense got a fourth-down stop. Sellers led a 61-yard drive and tied it with a run where he broke a number of tackles and reached the ball across the pylon. Then Dylan Stewart forced a fumble on a sack, and Tomiwa Durojaiye recovered it with 33 seconds left. Malik Orsan kicked a 48-yard field goal as time expired, and the fans stormed the field. Orsan was named SEC Special Teams Player of the Week, and center Nolan Hay was SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week.

Beau: (Full orchestra.) The music gets better every time I watch that kick.

Oklahoma won 23-15 at Mississippi State. Mateer went 22 of 29 for 283 yards and two touchdowns, and Sategna caught eight balls for 164 yards and a touchdown.

Injuries and availability

The first official SEC availability report for this game was due Wednesday. Oklahoma center Jake Maikkula got hurt at Mississippi State, and Caleb Nitta replaced him. Coach Brent Venables said Nitta could start at center if Maikkula isn't available. "He's a tough guy," Venables said.

There was happy news in Norman, too. Sooners player Sean Hutton had a health scare at practice and went to the hospital, and the team wore a helmet decal for him at Mississippi State. He was released and was waiting to greet the team when it got home. "It's a miracle, nothing short of that," Venables said. "I'm thankful for his health and for the doctors and the team that helped him through that episode."

Savannah: That one got me right in the heart, Beau.

Beau: Mine too. Turn the music down for that one. Amen.

What the coaches are up to

Shane Beamer is in his sixth season at South Carolina, and he knows Oklahoma well. He coached on Lincoln Riley's staff in Norman from 2018 to 2020. His team has beaten two straight ranked opponents, at Florida 38-19 and Tennessee.

Venables wants a cleaner offense. "Again, just get out of our own way and execute with great precision," he said. He also praised Sellers, Stewart and wide receiver Nyck Harbor. "Because of the dynamic ability of their playmakers, you have to know where everybody is."

Player storylines

These teams have met twice, and each has won once. In 2024, South Carolina won 35-9 in Norman, with a school-record nine sacks. Last year, Oklahoma won 26-7 in Columbia, and the Sooners had six sacks.

Stewart's forced fumble against Tennessee was the ninth of his career, which tied the South Carolina school record held by Jadeveon Clowney.

What's happening on campus

Memorial Stadium seats 80,126, and the Sooner Schooner will roll. Oklahoma claims seven national championships and seven Heisman Trophy winners, and the Sooners hold the Division I record with 47 straight wins.

South Carolina brings a proud history too, with George Rogers winning the 1980 Heisman Trophy.

Anything else fun and true

South Carolina is one of 13 FBS teams with more than one set of brothers on the roster. LaNorris Sellers shares the roster with his brother, wide receiver Jayden Sellers.

Savannah: Brothers on the same team. That's sweet, Beau.

Beau: Cue the family music, Savannah. Happy Halloween, Norman.

My call: Oklahoma Sooners 26, South Carolina Gamecocks 21.

Halloween in Happy Valley: Purdue Visits Penn State

Purdue (3-4, 2-2 Big Ten) at Penn State (3-4, 0-4 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4:15 p.m. ET, Beaver Stadium, University Park, Pennsylvania, BTN.

Your hosts are Barnaby Wolcott-Reese, a West Lafayette native and mechanical engineer who built a model Boilermaker Special in his garage, and Luann Kessler, a former Penn State volleyball setter who loves Creamery ice cream and linebackers equally.

Barnaby: Boiler up, Luann! I measured the drive from West Lafayette. Every mile was worth it.

Luann: We Are glad you came, Barnaby. Bring an appetite. The Creamery is open.

Players to watch

Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne has completed 145 of 221 throws for 1,822 yards, with 10 touchdowns and only three interceptions. Running back Fame Ijeboi has 568 yards and nine touchdowns on 130 carries. Wide receiver Asaad Waseem has 38 catches for 588 yards. Linebacker Jojo Hayden leads the defense with 48 tackles.

Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht has completed 132 of 210 throws for 1,664 yards and 12 touchdowns. Wide receiver Chase Sowell has 34 catches for 510 yards. Running back Carson Hansen has four rushing touchdowns. Linebacker Tony Rojas does a little of everything, with 55 tackles, five sacks and two interceptions.

Luann: Tony Rojas is mint chocolate chip. Cool, smooth and everywhere.

What happened last week

Both teams had a bye. Purdue last played on Oct. 16 and lost 38-26 to Washington at home. Browne threw for 273 yards, and Waseem caught nine balls for 116 yards.

Penn State last played on Oct. 17 and lost 21-18 at Michigan. Becht went 28 of 44 for 267 yards, and Sowell had a big day with 11 catches for 151 yards and a touchdown.

Barnaby: Eleven catches at the Big House. That young man earned his ice cream.

Injuries and availability

No official Big Ten availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Penn State wide receiver Koby Howard has missed the last four games with an undisclosed injury. He returned to practice and is considered questionable for Saturday.

Luann: Praying Koby gets back to full speed, whenever that is.

What the coaches are up to

Matt Campbell is in his first season at Penn State, and he brought Becht with him from Iowa State. After the Michigan game, Campbell made it clear Becht is his quarterback. "We have complete faith in Rocco," he said. "Rocco has continued to obviously play good football." Penn State is still looking for its first Big Ten win under Campbell.

Barry Odom is in his second season at Purdue. The Boilermakers went 2-10 in 2025, so a 3-4 start with two Big Ten wins is real progress. They won 24-17 at Illinois and beat Minnesota 41-13.

Player storylines

Both teams are 3-4, and both want to get back to even. Penn State's four losses came by four, 21, eight and three points, so the Nittany Lions have been close in most of them.

Purdue opened the year with Browne going 23 of 29 for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State. He threw for 378 yards at UCLA, and the Boilermakers took Wake Forest to overtime before losing 38-36.

Becht started his season in style, going 13 of 18 for 271 yards and four touchdowns in a 45-0 win over Marshall.

Barnaby: That's the blueprint, Luann. Draw it up, then build it.

What's happening on campus

Beaver Stadium holds 106,572. The field is West Shore Home Field, and the Penn State Blue Band will be out in force. Penn State claims national championships from 1982 and 1986, and the White Out is the tradition every visitor should see once.

Purdue's Ross-Ade Stadium opened in 1924. The Boilermaker Special is the tradition Barnaby would show you first, and the Purdue All-American Marching Band makes the trip a treat.

Anything else fun and true

Penn State's defense allows only 18.9 points a game. Purdue scores 31.3 a game. That's a fun matchup on Halloween afternoon.

Luann: Final Creamery Rankings this week, Barnaby. Your offense is rocky road.

Barnaby: I'll take that as a compliment, Luann. Boiler up.

My call: Penn State Nittany Lions 34, Purdue Boilermakers 23.

Kenzie Rhee is framing the Rose Bowl through her fingers like a camera when Ridge Corbell walks up in a snowboard jacket, squinting at the sunshine. "No powder in Pasadena?" he asks. Kenzie lowers her hands. "Darling, this is a movie set, not a ski lodge." Ridge grins. "Then let's send it, Kenzie. Roll camera."

Nevada (3-4, 2-2 Mountain West) visits No. 7 UCLA (7-0, 5-0 Big Ten) Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET on BTN at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena. DraftKings has UCLA Bruins −22.5 with a total of 44.5. On Monday, DraftKings had UCLA −23.5 and 48.5. My card: Nevada Wolf Pack +22.5, Over 44.5, and a final of UCLA Bruins 34, Nevada Wolf Pack 14.

Ridge speaks for Nevada. "We beat San José State 28-13 last week. Luke Duncan threw two touchdowns with no turnovers, and he spent his first three college seasons at UCLA. Our leading rusher has 582 yards and five touchdowns, and EJ Smith has 76 tackles. Coach Jeff Choate wants to keep this close into the fourth quarter. Sick."

Kenzie speaks for UCLA. "We beat Michigan State 28-10, darling. Ty Dieffenbach threw a touchdown, and Anthony Woods ran for 112 yards. Nico Iamaleava is out for the season after a knee injury at Oregon, so Ty is our lead now. Wayne Knight has 12 rushing touchdowns, Sammy Omosigho has five and a half sacks, and Jalen Woods has 59 tackles."

Why Nevada? Because 22.5 is a lot of points for a UCLA offense that has slowed down. In their last three games, the Bruins won 17-15 at Oregon, 17-7 against Wisconsin and 28-10 against Michigan State. Nevada runs the ball and can shorten the game. My final has UCLA winning by 20, short of 22.5.

The risk is Nevada's quarterback room. Carter Jones and AJ Bianco both missed last week, and Choate hasn't said who will start. Nevada also lost 20-7 at home to Montana State and 31-17 at North Dakota State. If the Wolf Pack turn it over, UCLA's defense could put this away early.

Why the Over? UCLA has scored 45 at Cal, 52 against Purdue and 54 at Maryland, and Knight finds the end zone almost every week. Nevada scored 49 against Western Kentucky and 33 against Air Force. The total has dropped from where it opened, but I think UCLA still gets there. My 34-14 adds up to 48, over 44.5.

Now the room. The Formula has UCLA 34-15 and likes Nevada and the Over. Next Man Up has UCLA 34-13, sides with Nevada, and likes the Over. Follow The Money likes Nevada after the spread came down a point, and likes the Under after the total fell. In The Trenches sits out: the Nevada run game and the UCLA run game each have a matchup they like, so they cancel out.

Follow The Money started it: "The total dropped. I go Under."

The Formula fired back: "UCLA scores 34 by itself. Over."

Next Man Up said: "UCLA wins big, just not that big."

Bottom of the card: an unbeaten UCLA team with a new quarterback, a Nevada team with a quarterback question and a Halloween crowd at the Rose Bowl. Give me the Wolf Pack and the Over.

UCLA Bruins 34, Nevada Wolf Pack 14. Nevada Wolf Pack cover the 22.5. Over 44.5.

Snowboards and Storyboards: Nevada Visits No. 7 UCLA on Halloween

Nevada (3-4, 2-2 Mountain West) at No. 7 UCLA (7-0, 5-0 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4:15 p.m. ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena, Calif., BTN.

Your hosts are Ridge Corbell, a Nevada fan, Tahoe ski patroller and snowboarder whose motto is "Send It," and Kenzie Rhee, a UCLA fan and Westwood film-school producer who storyboards every drive.

Kenzie: Welcome to Pasadena, Ridge! Sunshine, mountains in the distance and an unbeaten team. I'd greenlight it.

Ridge: Thanks, Kenzie. Those mountains have no snow on them, but I'll allow it.

Kenzie: This week's logline: "Mountain team visits the movie set."

Ridge: And the mountain team sends it. Strap in.

Players to watch

UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach has thrown the most passes in the last two games. He went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in his first start against Wisconsin and 18 of 31 for 198 yards and a touchdown against Michigan State. Wayne Knight leads the rushers with 627 yards and 12 touchdowns, and Semaj Morgan leads the receivers with 31 catches for 383 yards. Linebacker Sammy Omosigho has five and a half sacks, and Jalen Woods leads the defense with 59 tackles.

Nevada's Luke Duncan threw the most passes last week, going 18 of 29 for 178 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers. Carter Jones leads the team with 654 passing yards. Nevada's top running back has 582 yards and five touchdowns, and Gary Givens III leads the receivers with 19 catches for 305 yards. Linebacker EJ Smith leads the defense with 76 tackles, and Dylan LaBarbera has four sacks.

Kenzie: Wayne Knight has 12 rushing touchdowns. That's a franchise, darling.

Ridge: EJ Smith has 76 tackles. That dude never stops carving.

What happened last week

UCLA beat Michigan State 28-10 on Homecoming at the Rose Bowl, where the Bruins honored their 1966 Rose Bowl team. Anthony Woods ran 14 times for 112 yards and a touchdown, and Brian Rowe Jr. caught three balls for 74 yards and a score.

Kenzie: Homecoming, a callback to 1966 and a win. And. scene.

Nevada beat San José State 28-13 on Homecoming at Mackay Stadium. Duncan threw two touchdowns, and Marshaun Brown caught five balls for 52 yards and a score.

Ridge: Sick! I mimed a backflip. Nobody got hurt.

Injuries and availability

The official availability reports haven't been posted yet. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is out for the season after a knee injury in the Oregon game. For Nevada, starting quarterback Carter Jones (arm) and AJ Bianco (ankle) both missed last week, and coach Jeff Choate said it was too early to say who will start. Check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Bob Chesney is in his first season at UCLA, with a hire date of Dec. 6, 2025. He's a Dickinson College graduate who was head coach at Salve Regina, Assumption, Holy Cross and James Madison, and at Holy Cross he won five straight Patriot League titles. He's the first UCLA coach to begin his tenure 6-0, and the Bruins have kept on winning.

Jeff Choate was hired at Nevada on Dec. 4, 2023. This week he said his goal is to keep the game close: "Let's just drag this thing into deep water and find out who's gonna swim in the fourth quarter."

Kenzie: Coach Chesney walked onto the set and made a blockbuster. Breakout debut.

Ridge: Coach Choate wants deep water. I'm a snow guy, but I'm in.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Nevada's run game against a UCLA defense that allows 15.3 points a game. Duncan, if he plays, has a story all his own: he spent his first three college seasons at UCLA. On the other side, Knight and UCLA's big guys up front face a Nevada defense that has had trouble stopping the run. This is just the 10th time Nevada has played a top-10 team since moving up to the top level of college football.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween at the Rose Bowl, listed at 88,565 seats, one week after UCLA's Homecoming. Back in Reno, Nevada fans just celebrated Homecoming Week and the football program's 130th birthday, since the team was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers.

Kenzie: I'm dressing as a director's chair. Very supportive.

Ridge: I'm dressing as a snowboard. Pasadena needs a little winter.

Anything else fun and true

UCLA has been ranked in the AP top 10 at least once in every decade since the poll began in the 1930s, and the Bruins won the 1954 Coaches' Poll national title under Red Sanders. Nevada's Mackay Stadium field sits 4,610 feet above sea level, and Chris Ault, Frank Hawkins and Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame.

Ridge: Whatever happens, Kenzie, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Kenzie: Deal, darling. I'll bring dessert.

My call: UCLA Bruins 34, Nevada Wolf Pack 14.

display.story_text:
Zeb Coldiron whittles on a Watauga County porch and calls every drive a hike. Royce Ogeechee grew up in Bulloch County hearing his granddad tell stories about the old Eagles dynasty. On Halloween night in Statesboro, these old rivals meet for the forty-second time, and the East Division is on the table.

App State (5-2) at Georgia Southern (3-4), Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Allen E. Paulson Stadium in Statesboro. It's a Sun Belt game. DraftKings has Georgia Southern Eagles −5.5 with a total of 56.5. Action Network opened Georgia Southern −3.5 with a total of 54.5. My card: Georgia Southern Eagles −5.5, Under 56.5, and a final of Georgia Southern Eagles 29, App State Mountaineers 23.

Royce speaks for Georgia Southern. "Hail Southern! Max Johnson hurt his throwing shoulder at Old Dominion, and he's questionable. Clay Helton says the rehab progressed pretty fast, and Johnson walked out there and spun it. Turner Helton went 23 of 30 in relief, and we won 23-15. Anthony Bynum was Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week. And we've had sixteen days to rest up."

Zeb speaks for App State. "Come on up the mountain. Malachi Singleton went 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns in our overtime win over James Madison. Jaquari Lewis has 8 rushing touchdowns, and Caleb Sandstrom has 5 sacks. But steady footing matters. We scored three points against Old Dominion."

Here is the part that matters. Both teams are 2-1 in the league, tied for second in the East. Georgia Southern gives up 23.0 points a game, and App State gives up 23.1. Neither run game has found much room.

Why Georgia Southern? Follow The Money likes the Eagles after a two-point move, from −3.5 to −5.5. Next Man Up has Georgia Southern 30-22. Clay Helton is four and one against App State, and the Eagles lead the series in Statesboro thirteen to six. They're also unbeaten on Halloween.

Your hosts are Zeb Coldiron, a fourth-generation Watauga County whittler who treats every week like a hike, and Royce Ogeechee, a Bulloch County farm kid who grew up hearing about the Eagles' dynasty years from his granddad.

Zeb: Come on down off the mountain, Royce. I brought a jacket for your grandma.

Royce: Hail Southern, Zeb! She says thank you, and she says the Eagles are 4-0 on Halloween.

Players to watch

App State quarterback Malachi Singleton has completed 139 of 209 throws for 1,700 yards, with nine touchdowns and just two interceptions. Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks, and linebacker Colton Phares leads with 51 tackles.

Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson has thrown for 1,601 yards, with 11 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Wide receiver Alex Taylor has 24 catches for 342 yards. Linebacker Anthony Bynum has four sacks, and linebacker Brandon Tyson has 38 tackles.

Zeb: Two interceptions each. Those are careful young men.

What happened last week

App State beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. Singleton went 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns, and Nate Branch caught six balls for 73 yards.

Georgia Southern had a bye. In its last game, on Oct. 15, the Eagles won 23-15 at Old Dominion. Turner Helton came in for Johnson and went 23 of 30 for 206 yards and a touchdown. Bynum had three tackles for loss, two sacks and a forced fumble, and he was named Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week.

Royce: That's a farm-strong day's work from Anthony.

Zeb: Praying both quarterbacks are healthy. A rivalry deserves its best.

Clay Helton, who led USC to a Rose Bowl title, is 4-1 against App State. His son, Turner, is the backup quarterback who won the Old Dominion game. Georgia Southern has had 16 days to rest and get healthy.

Dowell Loggains is in his second season in Boone. He came from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator, and before that he called plays in the NFL for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets.

Here's a fun one. Johnson's father, Brad, and App State backup Henry Hasselbeck's father, Matt, both played in the NFL, and they played in two games against each other, in 2004 and 2006.

Georgia Southern lineman Colin Alexander said a win over App State would make the team "really, really confident" about reaching the conference championship.

Royce: That's the goal, Zeb. A conference title game.

Allen E. Paulson Stadium opened in 1984 and holds 25,000. Ask anybody about Beautiful Eagle Creek, and the Southern Pride Marching Band will be in full voice.

App State won three straight FCS national championships from 2005 to 2007. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do it.

Zeb: Three straight titles, Royce. That's a mountain worth the climb.

This is the 42nd meeting. App State leads the series 21-19-1, but Georgia Southern leads 13-6 in Statesboro. The teams have played every year since 1993, and these two programs are tied for second in the East Division.

Zeb: Steady climbing, honest footing, Royce. Then a view at the top.

Royce: Hail Southern, Zeb. The creek is calling.

Halloween Night in Ames: No. 24 Oklahoma State Visits Iowa State

Oklahoma State (5-2, 3-1 Big 12) at Iowa State (3-4, 1-3 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET (6:00 p.m. CT), Jack Trice Stadium, Ames, Iowa, FS1.

Your hosts are Dusty Lockridge, an Oklahoma State fan and ag-econ grad who explains offense with rodeo timing, and Twyla Hemmingsen, an Iowa State fan who forecasts every Saturday from her kitchen weather center.

Twyla: Good evening, Cyclone Nation! Tonight's forecast: cold front from the south, wearing orange.

Dusty: Orange from my hat to my boots, Twyla. We're riding into Ames for the full eight seconds.

Players to watch

Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker has completed 157 of 239 throws for 2,326 yards, with 20 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's thrown for 300 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receiver Wyatt Young has 36 catches for 639 yards and six scores. Running back Caleb Hawkins has 712 yards on 142 carries. Linebacker Ethan Wesloski leads the defense with 70 tackles and 3.5 sacks.

Iowa State running back Aiden Flora has 716 yards and six touchdowns on 102 carries. Quarterback Jaylen Raynor has thrown for 1,107 yards and seven touchdowns. Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has 71 tackles, and defensive end Isaac Terrell has three sacks.

Twyla: Flora is the jet stream. Watch the radar.

What happened last week

Oklahoma State beat Colorado 57-24 at home. Mestemaker went 21 of 36 for 386 yards and four touchdowns. Justin Bowick caught five balls for 138 yards and a score, and Hawkins ran for 120 yards.

Iowa State lost 39-3 at No. 22 Arizona. Raynor fumbled late in the first half, and Jimmy Rogers gave backup Connor Moberly the second half to look for a spark. Flora was held to 36 yards.

Dusty: Tough night in the desert. Those Cyclones will come home hungry.

Injuries and availability

No official Big 12 availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Oklahoma State safety Mose Phillips hurt his shoulder against UCF and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Safety Quinton Hammonds was hurt recovering a fumble against Colorado and came back to the sideline in a sling. "Hopeful that we can get Q back," Eric Morris said.

Dusty: Prayers for Mose and Q. Good young men, both of them.

What the coaches are up to

Jimmy Rogers settled the quarterback question early. "We're gonna go with Jaylen," he said, calling Raynor "the best leader on the team." Raynor will make his 43rd straight start, counting his time at Arkansas State. Rogers also said of Moberly, "his future's bright."

Eric Morris is in his first season in Stillwater. Mestemaker and Hawkins followed him from North Texas, and the Cowboys are No. 24 in the country after going 1-11 last season.

Iowa State defensive coordinator Jesse Bobbit was honest about the challenge. "He can make the throws," he said of Mestemaker. "You can see it on tape."

Player storylines

Mestemaker ran 75 yards on one play in the 39-31 win over Oregon. That one run is half of his season rushing total.

Raynor is one of six team captains, elected by his teammates in the preseason. When he was benched, he spent the second half coaching up and cheering on Moberly.

Twyla: That's a captain. Sunshine in the forecast for that young man.

What's happening on campus

Jack Trice Stadium holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete, and it got his name in 1997. It is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every visitor should know his story.

Oklahoma State has played football since 1901. The Cowboys claim the 1945 national championship, and Barry Sanders won the Heisman Trophy in 1988.

Anything else fun and true

This is Iowa State's fifth game against a ranked team in its first eight. The Cyclones are 3-1 at home this season, and their home wins include a 45-42 thriller over West Virginia.

Dusty: I'll bring the stopwatch, Twyla. You bring the forecast.

Twyla: Barometer's falling, Dusty. That's Cyclone weather.

My call: Oklahoma State Cowboys 30, Iowa State Cyclones 27.

Cougars and Aztecs Meet Under the San Diego Lights

Washington State (1-7, 0-4 Pac-12) at San Diego State (3-5, 2-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET (4:00 p.m. Pacific), Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego, CBSSN.

Your hosts are Hank Palouse, a Washington State fan who drives a combine and keeps a shoebox of game tapes in the cab, and Kai Delgado-Sorensen, a San Diego State fan who surfs Ocean Beach most mornings.

Kai: Welcome to sunshine, Hank. You can leave the combine at home.

Hank: Brought the shoebox, though. Cougs never quit.

Players to watch

Washington State quarterback Owen Eshelman has started the last two games. Caden Pinnick, who started the first six, has thrown for 952 yards. Wide receiver Branden Ganashamoorthy leads the team with 30 catches for 401 yards and three touchdowns, and Kirby Vorhees has 275 rushing yards. On defense, linebacker Keith Brown has 60 tackles, and defensive tackle Jirah Leaupepetele has 2.5 sacks.

San Diego State quarterback Stone Saunders, a redshirt freshman and Kentucky transfer, gets his second straight start. Running back Javion Kinnard leads the team with 526 rushing yards. Wide receiver Jaylon Hawkins has 322 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Linebacker Sione Hala has 83 tackles, and linebacker Djibril Rahman has 3.5 sacks.

Kai: Hala's in on every play. That's a surfer who never gets out of the water.

What happened last week

Washington State lost 31-10 at home to Boise State. Eshelman completed 21 throws for 191 yards and ran the ball 23 times. Ganashamoorthy and Daniel Blood played all 76 snaps on offense.

San Diego State lost 56-49 at Colorado State in a wild one. The 105 combined points were the most in a game in San Diego State's Division I history. Saunders went 23 of 33 for 369 yards and two touchdowns in his first college start. Hawkins caught six balls for a career-high 164 yards and scored a touchdown for the fifth straight game. Lucky Sutton ran for 98 yards and two scores, and Kinnard added two more on just 10 carries.

Hank: One hundred sixty-four yards for Hawkins. That one's going in the shoebox, even if he's not ours.

Injuries and availability

No official Pac-12 availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Coach Kirby Moore said wide receiver Darrius Clemons (ankle) and safety Jeremiah Bernard (shoulder) are day-to-day and set to return to practice this week. For San Diego State, Jayden Denegal remains day-to-day.

What the coaches are up to

Moore is in his first season at Washington State. He wants sharper practices this week. "We talk about deliberate practice," he said. "That really starts with bringing great energy, having verbal combat, doing your assignment, making sure you're not thinking out there, that you're just reacting."

Sean Lewis is in his third season at San Diego State. He named Saunders the starter on Monday. "Stone will start this week," Lewis said. "So, he'll get the bulk of the one reps as we go forward."

Kai: Clear call from the coach. Gnarly.

Player storylines

Saunders came into his first start with just 15 career throws. His 369 yards were the most ever by an Aztec quarterback making his first start on the road, going back to 1969. He also became the first Aztec to throw for 300 yards since Jalen Mayden in the 2022 Hawai'i Bowl.

Ganashamoorthy has played 503 snaps this season, the most of any wide receiver in the Pac-12. Washington State's only win so far came 48-7 over Duquesne, and the Cougars lost 17-16 at Utah State. They're looking for their first win over an FBS team.

Hank: One-point loss. I've watched it twice. Still hurts.

What's happening on campus

Snapdragon Stadium opened in 2022 and seats 35,000. San Diego State began playing football in 1921 and has won 21 conference championships.

Washington State is in Pullman, where the first Cougar team took the field in 1894. Home is Martin Stadium, which opened in 1972 on ground that dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field.

Anything else fun and true

The Aztecs went 9-4 last year and are trying to get to a bowl game for a second straight season. They have won two close home games this year, 31-29 over Texas State and 26-23 over Fresno State.

Hank: Ganashamoorthy, five hundred and three snaps. That young man has earned a nap.

Kai: Bring him to the beach after, Hank. Respect.

My call: San Diego State Aztecs 27, Washington State Cougars 25.
